reviews.author: Wayne Flint
reviews.text:
★★★★★

Radiant Plumbing 🪠 serviced my home today and I couldn’t be more satisfied with the experience. They fixed a severely clogged double kitchen sink quickly and thoroughly. From start to finish, the service was professional, courteous, and honest.

A special shoutout to Garrett, the plumbing professional who handled the job—he was polite, knowledgeable, and took the time to explain exactly what was going on and how he resolved it. You can tell he brings years of real hands-on experience to his work, and it shows in the quality of the repair.

On top of excellent service, the pricing was very fair, and I was given a 6-month warranty, which gave me even more confidence in the work performed.

If you’re looking for a trustworthy plumbing company that stands behind their service, I highly recommend Radiant Plumbing. They earned every bit of this 5-star review.

reviews.author: Kevin Conboy
reviews.text:
I had a major hot water heater leak at my Airbnb on a Saturday night, and Radiant Plumbing responded immediately. Their dispatch team had me scheduled right away, and Marcel, a Master Plumber, arrived early Sunday morning.

From the moment he started diagnosing the problem, it was clear Marcel knew exactly what he was doing. He quickly determined that my water heater needed replacement and recommended replacing both units since they were the same age and installed in tandem. He also identified plumbing that had been installed incorrectly and explained how to bring everything up to code.

Marcel presented several options without pressure, clearly explaining the pros and cons of each. I chose two Marathon water heaters, and by that evening the entire installation was complete, including all new plumbing.

Marcel was professional, knowledgeable, courteous, and took the time to explain everything throughout the process. The quality of the work was outstanding. I highly recommend Radiant Plumbing and especially Marcel for anyone looking for honest advice, expert workmanship, and exceptional service.

reviews.text:

We'll definitely be using him for our plumbing project. If you're buying a house or need plumbing work done, I highly recommend Jeff because he is the guy.

reviews.author: Alyson Gilkerson
reviews.text:
We used these guys a few years ago and it was great. However, recently we had a mystery leak and the experience was miserable.

They didn’t detect the leak the first time around, which I can understand. Had them come back, they found the leak. Repaired it and changed the plumbing on a sink that supposedly wasn’t plumbed right, but wasn’t causing any issues. We had water remediation come and dry everything out.

The leak they repaired continued to leak. It took several days for them to send someone to fix it again. They didn’t show up to one appointment because they couldn’t get ahold of me - but I didn’t receive any calls or texts to confirm, so I don’t know what that was about.

A few days later the sink they “fixed” (that we never had issues with before) started pouring water. Gallons all over the bathroom….and back out the ceiling below, that we just paid to have dried out. They sent someone else to come fix the sink again. We had to pay again to have everything dried out to prevent mold.

I asked about compensation for the second dry out, since it was entirely caused by something they did. I was told the owner would call me. I never received a call, despite trying to follow up several times over the course of a week. I eventually got so frustrated I decided to just eat the cost and won’t be using them again.

reviews.author: Holly
reviews.text:
I am updating my review after further follow-up with customer service, and my concerns were not resolved. At this point, I am no longer pursuing a refund.

My experience with Reliant Plumbing was extremely disappointing. The pricing felt excessive for the quality of work provided, and the service did not reflect what was promised or expected.

The technician assigned to my job, Mark Allen, did not complete the work in a way that resolved the issue. What initially appeared to be a fixed problem later proved to still be unresolved, resulting in additional frustration and time lost.

I also have serious concerns about the authenticity of the positive reviews. I was told by others that employees may receive incentives tied to positive reviews they generate. I cannot confirm this, but it raised legitimate concerns for me about how some of the reviews here are obtained.

Based on my personal experience, I cannot recommend Reliant Plumbing. I strongly encourage others to get multiple estimates, ask detailed questions before work begins, and carefully verify the scope of service being provided. My experience did not reflect professionalism, transparency, or quality workmanship.

What should have been a simple repair turned into an expensive and frustrating situation that I would not want others to go through..

• Very disappointing experience with Reliant Plumbing, specifically with technician Mark Allen. What should have been a straightforward repair turned into a long, drawn-out visit. He left at one point to retrieve parts and later returned stating he had replaced the flush valve and replaced the commode. I initially held off on leaving a review until I had another plumber inspect the work. After that second evaluation, I was informed that the commode was actually cracked and had not been properly replaced or addressed. It appeared the original fixture had simply been cleaned, polished, and reinstalled rather than replaced as stated. Based on the follow-up assessment and overall experience, I will not be using this company again and do not recommend their services.

reviews.text:
We paid over $6,000 for a new water heater. The replacement unit began showing ignition errors instantly and we have been without reliable hot water for several days. We have had plumbers show up multiple times and a roofer and still no change. Multiple requests for manager follow-up have gone unanswered. We are hopeful the company will respond and resolve the issue.

Update: UPDATE (5 days later):

I appreciate Reliant’s public response. Unfortunately, since posting my original review, we still do not have reliable hot water.

We paid over $6,000 for a new Navien tankless water heater after our previous unit failed. The replacement unit immediately began experiencing ignition errors, and we have now gone approximately 11 days without hot water.

Since installation, Reliant has sent technicians to our home numerous times, including management involvement, multiple troubleshooting visits, venting modifications, and other diagnostic work. Despite these efforts, the problem remains unresolved.

What is most frustrating is that the public response asks me to contact the office and request a manager, which I have already done repeatedly throughout this process. At this point, I am simply asking for a functioning water heater, reliable hot water, and consistent communication regarding a resolution.

I will gladly update this review again if and when the issue is fully resolved.

reviews.author: William Chernik
reviews.text:
My experience is 2 stars only because I never felt comfortable enough (and was too frustrated) to allow them to service my home.

My hot water heater stopped working two days ago. Pilot light kept going out and I couldn't even get the burner to turn on.

I called the same day as the issue and scheduled service for the morning of the next day. My spouse adjusted work plans to be home. It got late into the afternoon and we didn't receive a call. Finally, I called them and their dispatcher said they needed to push service to the next day.

The next day, I took the day off of work, the plumber shows up, I tell him the symptoms and he starts saying I probably need a whole new unit. He didn't even troubleshoot at this point! Didn't put hands or eyes on the unit. I had to coax him into looking at the water heater and coming up with a diagnosis.

After looking at the unit for all of 20 seconds, he starts telling me how it's from home depot and he can't even really give me an estimate for the control valve change. I needed to, once again, coax him into a solution because he just wasn't giving me anything! He really seemed like he just didn't want to do the work, wasting my time and my spouse's time. I finally got him to at least quote me on a new water heater. It was like pulling teeth to get him to take my money.

When people call a plumbing service, they have lost a utility that is severely impacting their everyday life. The plumber acted like I was wasting his time by asking him to help fix my issue. Between the scheduling and the response from the plumber, I did not feel comfortable using their plumbing services.

Giving them the benefit of the doubt, the first day I got rescheduled was crazy busy for them and the plumber that showed up was having a bad day or was just a bad apple. Not sure. But this was not a pleasant experience. Maybe they do amazing work! But I never even got to that point...

reviews.author: Matt Riopelle
reviews.text:
Roto-Rooter is performing the fix and remediation for water damage from a pipe leak behind the shower.

On-site, the technicians are great. It's fast and quality work and they know how to communicate with customers.

The low star rating is for scheduling communication and not following through on promised time-frames.

After first assessment of the issue, which occurred in the afternoon, they promised to be back first thing in the morning to begin work. Well, morning came and went without a call or update. I began calling, and was promised three different times that someone would call me back right away. Those calls also never happend.

Finally, at 4:30pm, someone called and said a tech had an unexpected injury and nobody couldn't make it out that day. They did promise to start at 9:30am the next morning. I was promised this time by both a supervisor and a dispatcher.

That time again came and went without a call or update. At 11:30am, the tech called and said they'd be there about 2:30pm. This time, they actually did show, though it wasn't until later.

In addition, they needed to come back and check moisture levels every day. I would receive a call about 30 minutes beforehand and if I wasn't available, they wouldn't do the reading for that day.

I don't know how a business runs this way. How disrespectful to your customer's time and plans. I understand things happen. And that's when you update the customer so they aren't left in the dark. A few timely phone calls and I wouldn't be writing this negative review.

I can't recommend Roto-Rooter to anyone who expects a service provider to show up when they say they will.

Update: It’s been eight weeks since they started and the work is still not finished. Not once have they showed up when they said they would. They ordered the wrong carpet, so as of today, there’s still exposed subfloor.

reviews.author: Carolyn Byczek
reviews.text:
Update: Despite the owner responding below I never heard from them. It has been a nightmare even getting info on HOW to pay at this point while only receiving warnings on property liens, etc. I would absolutely never use Roto-Rooter again.

I had a kitchen flood and because it was an active water loss situation, I understandably moved quickly with mitigation services. When the Roto-Rooter supervisor came out that evening he gave me a whole song and dance about how they would work with insurance, it would be fully covered, etc. while providing me with quite a large range of estimate. At certain points he even said he was quoting "high" so it would help the coverage.

The final invoice ended up being so dramatically higher than what my insurance company and their independent third-party reviewer determined was reasonable and customary for the work performed that they could not come to an agreement. Even after revisions, there remained a significant dispute regarding pricing and scope which I am responsible for. Throughout this process, I was caught in the middle between Roto-Rooter and Nationwide/Accuserve, despite having no meaningful involvement in directing the mitigation scope, equipment usage, or pricing decisions during the emergency response itself.

Communication from Roto-Rooter throughout the billing process was inconsistent and contradictory. I received multiple notices threatening collections activity, liens, and a Notice to Owner while the invoice was still actively under review and while the insurance company was in the process of issuing payment for the undisputed amount. This created a tremendous amount of unnecessary stress during an already difficult home restoration process.

My advice to anyone using emergency mitigation services is:

- Don't use this company
- Ask detailed questions about billing and insurance negotiations upfront especially as RotoRooter is known to "overcharge" insurance and when they don't pay make it the liability of the homeowner
- Request itemized documentation early
- Understand exactly what you are signing regarding payment responsibility
- Be prepared for potential disputes between mitigation vendors and insurance reviewers

I understand emergency mitigation work is expensive and time-sensitive, but I do not believe homeowners should be placed in the middle of prolonged billing disputes between vendors and insurers while simultaneously facing threats of collections or liens before the insurance review process has fully concluded.

The only bright spot were the technicians who actually did the work were professional, responsive, and seemed to know what they were doing.

I previously used this company for an exterior leak issue, and that experience was actually very positive. They were able to identify and resolve the problem successfully, which is why I trusted them again for this new issue.

Unfortunately, this recent experience was very disappointing and concerning.

I was told that my home failed a hydrostatic test and isolation test and was advised that major under-slab repair/tunneling (20 feet long) work was needed. The report was very simple without enough details. However, given the high cost for the repair, I later hired another licensed plumbing company for a second opinion. They performed both a full camera inspection and another hydrostatic test, with me personally present and observing the entire process from start to finish.

The second company found no visible pipe damage on camera inspection, and the hydrostatic test passed without any meaningful water level drop. Based on those results, there was no evidence of an active drain leak requiring repair.

Given the scale, cost, and invasive nature of the repair that was recommended to me, I expected a much higher level of certainty, documentation, and professionalism before being told that such major work was necessary.

I appreciate the good work they did for my previous exterior leak issue, but after this experience, I no longer feel confident trusting their diagnosis for major plumbing repairs.

reviews.author: Slade Gauntt
reviews.text:
Replaced two 50 gallon propane water heaters with a Navien 240A Tankless Unit.  Arnold from a deal plumbing took my call and came out following day to give me an estimate.   I had estimates from 5 different plumbers, price range between estimates was dramatic.  A deal plumbing was not the cheapest, but was very competitive across all the plumbers I contacted.  They were able to complete the install the day after I confirmed with them.

They spent time evaluating the gas supply/demand in my home to determine best approach for adding tankless water heater.  My original water heaters pulled 40K BTUS each (80K total) where the Navien can pull up to 200K BTUs, so it’s important to determine best connection to ensure ample supply to Tankless heater.  Some plumbers suggested just connecting new tankless to my existing ½ inch gas line, but most including A deal Plumbing suggested running new ¾ inch gas line to ensure adequate supply.  They took the time to run the new gas line underneath the subfloor in my walk-in attic (where original gas lines ran) so that it would be out of the way, and wouldn’t be stepped on by any traffic passing through the attic.

Arnold suggested using concentric venting so that the new unit could have direct intake/exhaust through existing vent hole in my roof.  Worked great and no roofing/flashing re-work was required.   We added new rubber gasket, which Arnold provided, over existing flashing which was a perfect solution.

Arnold followed up a fews days after the original install to ensure that everything was working properly.  I pointed out to him that the isolation kit A Deal Plumbing installed with the unit wasn’t Navien OEM and didn’t have shut-off valves where the flush hoses would connect.  Arnold evaluated and agreed this was a poor design and would be impractical when flushing.  He ordered the OEM parts and returned within 1 week to replace the original isolation kit.  He added extension pipe to the isolation kit valves to drop them below all the connections at base of heater so they would be easy to access during annual maintenance of the unit.

Natural Gas to LP Conversion requires dip switch configuration on the unit’s control panel which was overlooked during install, but easily remedied … just glad I checked. The model I purchased includes an internal circulation pump, which requires an internal valve to be switched when using dedicated return line, and some control panel dip switch configuration.  A Deal Plumbing didn’t seem familiar with these configurations for the embedded re-circulation pump, but I was able to read manual and easily configure myself.  They were very familiar with how to install the unit and are listed as a recommended installer on Navien’s website.

Arnold was hands on, involved and participating with his crew throughout the whole install.  He and his crew are very cool guys and easy to work with, which I very much appreciated.   Unit is working great in my home, am satisfied with the install and the tankless heater’s performance.

Tim also identified a potentially serious safety issue that had been caused by previous roofing work. A flue vent had become loose, creating a possible carbon monoxide hazard. Thank goodness he found it and corrected the issue before it became a bigger problem. That alone gave me tremendous confidence in his attention to detail and integrity.

Later, they replaced my nearly 15-year-old water heater. The installation was completed quickly and professionally, and Tim showed me everything he was doing and explained everything afterward. There was significant sediment buildup in the old unit, which confirmed that replacing it was the right decision. Again, there was no pressure to purchase upgrades or unnecessary equipment.

Karen maintained excellent communication throughout the entire process and followed up afterward to make sure everything was satisfactory. That level of customer care is rare these days.

By the end of the experience, I felt like I had known these people for years. They are genuine, trustworthy, and truly willing to go the extra mile for their customers. They also offer financing options and are happy to help you understand them without pressure.

This is now my plumbing company for life. If you want honest people, outstanding communication, quality work, and customer service that is second to none, I highly recommend them.

reviews.author: Hobby Perez
reviews.text: Huge thanks to Juan from Crows Plumbing Service for the great work today. You can tell he takes pride in doing things right and making customers feel comfortable. Folks like Juan make it easy to support local businesses—Crows Plumbing is lucky to have him.

reviews.author: Jillian Ross
reviews.text:
Juan did an excellent job installing and hooking up my water softener. He arrived on time, was professional, and clearly knew what he was doing. The installation was clean and efficient, and he even explained how the system works and what I should do for basic maintenance.

It’s not always easy to find someone reliable, but Juan definitely delivered. I really appreciate his attention to detail and the quality of his work. If you need plumbing work or a water softener installed, I highly recommend Juan!

reviews.author: Joyce Godfrey
reviews.text:
Let me start from the beginning, my call with Karen.  She was so delightful, I felt as if I was talking to a friend. I think we laughed the entire time while scheduling my appointment.  It was a welcoming experience. It's really nice to talk with someone who seems to enjoy their job with positive communication skills. We laughed during a stressful situation.
Juan called before he arrived and was very respectful and kind. He accessed our situation, explained two options in detail as to what had to be done to fix our bursted pipe. He showed my husband the completed task and explained what he had done. We really appreciate his professionalism. Overall, our experience with Crow's Plumbing was positive.

reviews.author: Juniper Land
reviews.text: I’ve been dealing with a complex ongoing sewer gas issue after my pump broke during a week of heavy storms that lead to more plumbing issues then just the pump and I cannot say enough good things about this company. First  they don’t have some automated attendant answering the phones but rather a real live person who also is engaged in wanting to truly help you. Karen who handles the calls is so helpful I know her by name. She went out of her way to really discuss things in such detail and follow up with me on multiple occasions that I knew this was a different kind of company - more old school integrity based type business. She explained they had someone with extensive background in these complex plumbing problems that still persist even after the first line repairs  who they dedicate to addressing these  type of complex plumbing issues who has been doing this work for years.  She connected me   David who was the single most knowledgeable  person I’ve talked to about these type of plumbing issues and he even made himself available by phone to talk to me about what was going on at my house after multiple successful repairs but where I was still struggling with sewer gas issues after the repairs, something I’ve never dealt with before in my home. So there are several reasons that I would recommend this company. They are genuinely committed to wanting to help you and they are wildly knowledgeable about complex plumbing issues beyond just fixing a standard problem. To find an ethical, caring knowledgeable company is such a rarity and triple win. I have never reviewed a company before they have even come out to do the work. But that is how positive and refreshing experience I’ve had with this company where the people are not  just kind and generous with their time but extremely knowledgeable. I am not a handy person and I was having to comb through Reddit posts and research the problems I was having on AI and David was the first person I talked to where I finally felt like someone was going to figure this out for me. Before finding Crows I had worked a while with another good plumber who did really  good work in getting a new pump set up for me after I had had repeated problems with a pump that had never been properly installed to begin with. I also realized though that sometimes you have to track down specialists for these more complex issues that involve more than one thing and persist even after a successful repair. So I’m so glad to have found this gem of a company.

reviews.author: Justice McDonald
reviews.text: Ethan with Abacus Plumbing came out right at 5pm and worked until 8pm to get our main water line repaired properly. He was knowledgeable, thorough, and took the time to make sure the repair was done right. Really appreciate his work ethic and expertise. Highly recommend asking for Ethan specifically.

reviews.author: Jason
reviews.text:
So I had 2 issues pop up over the holiday weekend.  AC went out on July 3rd (holiday), and was having some electrical issues with my outside breaker box.  AC Issue:  had a Thermostat wire die causing the BRAND NEW hvac system not to turn on  Friday July 3rd.  I called a millions places and only Abacus  had a emergency technician come out within 2 hours on a holiday, which is already amazing.  My normal AC place, who installed the new HVAC system and I have been using for 20 years wanted 300 bucks an hour to come out.  Abacus didnt charge a fee and was available in 2 hours.  Abel M should up and was polite and was able to troubleshoot my system.  Repairs were finished within an hour.  Abel walked us through everything he was doing and also stayed and answered questions we had.  I mentioned my lights were flickering as he was testing the AC and he mentioned they had electricians that could check it out and he would set up the appointment.  Amazing technician!!!!!!!

Breaker Box Issue:  As I was trouble shooting my AC not turning on, I flipped the outdoor breaker. When I turned the breaker back on, I noticed a sizzling inside the box. I mentioned this to the HVAC technician Able M.  Donny B was assigned to be my electrician.  Donny showed up on time and was polite. He immediatley checked the breaker box and already knew the issue.  Donny also found a few other issues with the ground wire and the AC amperage not matching the breakerbox amperage. Donny walked through everything he found wrong and told us what he thinks we should do.   He also recommened a whole house power surge protector, which I have been meaning to get with how amazing our Texas power grid is.  I beleive the surge protector is required on houses 2023 and newer nowbut dont quote me on that.

TLDR:  I recieved excellent service from Donny B and Abel M on a freaking holiday weekend.  Abacus certainly saved the holiday weekend for my family and we truly appreciate it.  Ive seen the reviews that they are "not the cheapest" and tend to "offer upsells", but my experience  was great and I would certainly use them again.

reviews.author: Justin LeVrier
reviews.text:
Treated poorly and egregiously overcharged by their crew, and there was nobody I could reach to talk about it that seemed to care, listen or want to try and help. From my experience, this company no longer stands behind their service nor cares about their customers. Please allow me to share...

After personally finding a small water leak outside our home, and digging a large hole around the source of a small outside water leak (small 1" elbow pipe coming out of the house - photo of my work attached), I recommended that my girlfriend call Good Flow Plumbing. After a few attempts to reach them, she left a message during business hours, then finally connected via text and booked an appointment (a few days out). On the appointment date, their crew arrived late, outside their 4 hour arrival window.

The good news; they fixed the leak, and did so in only 38 minutes! And that should be our happy ending – right?

Unfortunately for us, not a happy ending. This is the point where they presented my girlfriend with a bill for nearly $500 for their "time and materials". She asked how a 30 min job could be so expensive, (she was told to expect $200 max), and they said "digging holes are hard, and they cost more money." Of course this is nonsense, the hole was already dug, I dug it myself. Any extra digging, including the actual water leak fix was an elapsed grand total of 38 minutes.

Who charges $500 for 30 minutes of work? Are there plumbers in Austin charging $1,000 an hour now? Is there some sort of hazard pay for using a shovel that I should be aware of?

They tried to justify an inflated price to my girlfriend assuming she wouldn't know the difference. She did know the difference, but decided not to push back any further as she was home alone, and already feeling uncomfortable by the two mens presence, so she paid the bill when they asked her to pay.

When I returned home from Base, she relayed the story to me, and I said I would call their office and speak to management to let them know how their crew made her feel, and address the overcharge. Well, after repeated attempts to reach anyone at their office, I finally connected via text message, and eventually moved to a phone call. To my dismay, the lady who took the call (name starts with a J) was argumentative, defensive, and did not care to hear what I had to say nor help in any way.

The sad part; I previously referred Good Flow Plumbing to many friends in Austin, and cited their company as some of the best, most honest plumbers out there — not anymore.

I am currently shopping for another plumbing contractor to send my friends, family and personal business to.

I don’t get why anyone would be so shortsighted. Okay, so now they have an extra couple hundred dollars, and we have an experience. And now I’m sharing our experience so others don’t accidentally part ways with their hard earned dollars, for slow, poor service with zero respect.

reviews.author: Fritz Weiss
reviews.text:
On Saturday, May 3 we had a nasty plumbing issue.  Raw sewage backed up into the lower level of our house through a toilet and shower.  Super gross!  I start hauling stuff out of the house and using my shop vac, and calling plumbers and septic system companies trying to get someone to come help me ASAP.  The first company that I can reach who can send someone is LT Plumbing.  Maybe they are called Lake Travis Plumbing too...  Anyway the guy comes over pretty quickly.  He looks around the mess for two seconds and tells me "your septic tank is full and overflowing, and we don't do septic systems".  And then he charges me $185 for a trip charge and leaves.  Nothing was mentioned on the phone about them "not doing septic systems", but whatever...

I get back on the phone and start calling more septic system companies.  Finally get a realtor friend to talk to someone he knows, and get a crew over there in the early afternoon.  These guys open the lid to my septic tank and find that it is not full at all.  They find that there is a blockage in the drain line before it gets to the septic system.  Just the sort of thing LT Plumbing should be able to easily address.  They clear the blockage, charge me $150 and I go about the business of cleaning up the toxic waste.

After the weekend is over and the house is cleaned, I call LT Plumbing to explain to them what happened.  I sent them the receipt I got from the other septic company that noted it was not a septic system issue at all, just a blocked house drain line.  I felt like their guy should have at least checked the septic tank to confirm that it was overflowing, instead of just guessing.  I felt like I paid $185 for absolutely nothing.  LT Plumbing gave me the runaround for a week, promised to "look into", but basically they blew me off.  Called again today and was basically told "too bad".  So they are going to keep the $185 they took from me.

I will never call them again, and if anyone asks me I will tell them this story and strongly suggest that they call any other plumber in town besides LT Plumbing.  That is no way to run a business, and they should be ashamed of themselves!

Background of the Caswell House.

As you may or may not know, the Caswell House, located at 1404 West in downtown Austin, was built in 1899. Over the decades, it has changed ownership several times. Since 1978, the house has been under the stewardship of the Austin Junior Forum, a women’s service organization dedicated to supporting the most vulnerable members of our community—including women, children, and the elderly. The Caswell House allows us to host community events and raise funds in support of our 501(c)(3) mission.

I have been a member of the Austin Junior Forum since 2023 and have served as the building manager since late December 2024. In that time, I have interacted with every person who comes through our doors, including many service providers. Future Recommendations
I have complete trust in John and his team, and I will not hesitate to consult Fox for any future needs!

Thank you again!
Kelly Treybig – Manager Caswell House - Austin Junior Forum

reviews.author: Douglas Shea
reviews.text: I highly recommend Redbud Plumbing.  For years I've used their services at two Austin rent houses I manage, and at my home, as well. reviews.author: Marcus Villanueva
reviews.text:
This is the third time I've used Redbud and each time has been a great experience.  No nonsense, no upsales, no pressure, just knowledgeable professionals.

reviews.text:
If you’re looking for a plumbing company in Austin that is trustworthy, fair, efficient, and genuinely easy to work with, I highly recommend Proven Plumbing Austin. reviews.author: Sarah McCafferty
reviews.text: Had a good experience with Proven for HVAC repair. Their price for leak detection was much more affordable than the company I had been with. I'm not sure how it compares to others. Technician was very nice, timely and communicated well. The overall price of the service was quite expensive but again I have nothing to compare it to since I've never had this service before.

reviews.author: Neil Guayante
reviews.text:
Louis, the owner contacted me personally to address the situation described below. I can’t thank him enough for his persistence, and his response more than made up for the issue we had.  While our first call wasn’t a great experience, I have no doubt Louis will ensure the next one is. I think what happened was a fluke, as everyone speaks so highly of Proven. Thank you, Louis!

Hired Proven to do a bi-annual HVAC check up.  We were scheduled for 2-5pm.  I got notice at 4pm the tech was on his way.  He didn't show up until right at 5pm. I warned him we had been dealing with noises in our house, I knew he was there to clean the units and not to fix any problems.  He didn't listen real well, and told me he'd have to charge $225 an hour to work on it.  I told him I didn't ask him out to work on that noise.  I just wanted him to know about it.  He asked what the noise sounded like, so I played a video for him.  He immediately told me it was "water hammer".  I told him I already tried fixing that by turning the main water off and emptying the pipes.  The noise kept going. He said, "That's 100% water hammer".  He told me in a VERY long-winded way that I didn't drain the pipes correctly and I needed to fill all the faucets slowly to remove the air.  He talked a LOT.  If I inserted anything he didn't pay attention. He knew it all. His van said A/C and Plumbing...so I listened.  Maybe I got it wrong.  I told him I had family coming for dinner, and didn't have a lot of time.  But I turned off the water again and drained every single faucet and bath.  He told me to wait 30 minutes.  I didn't have time, so I waited 20 and started filling.  After about an hour, the water main was back on and the noises were still there.  He had wasted an hour and a half of my time.  He even played water hammer sounds for me from a Youtube video....the sounds were nowhere near as loud as the sounds in the house that he INSISTED were water hammer.  He then told me he spoke to his plumbing manager and said the plumbing manager would call me the next day.  Nobody called.  No follow up.  I went outside the next day and found my water hose disconnected and in a pile by the faucet.  He hadn't put it back on.  When I started it up, the hose was broken and leaking at the connection.  I fill my pool weekly and it was working fine before.  It was a fairly new hose. So I had to buy a new 100ft hose. Just a poor experience all around.  That, and the company I had before would spend a good 2-3 hours cleaning my HVAC system.  This guy took maybe an hour in between talking a lot.  He is a really nice guy, but didn't listen well, didn't clean up or hang the hose like I had it and wasted a good hour of water I had running to slowly fill up my pipes again. Listening to clients first, acknowledging what they say and THEN responding would be a good lesson for him.

reviews.author: Rabih C
reviews.text:

reviews.author: Tracey Stanton

The whole plumbing repair took about three days, and I was kept updated during each step of the process so I always knew what was happening next. They cleaned up carefully after every visit and left the work area in excellent shape. reviews.author: Aurora Callahan

reviews.author: San Zeng
reviews.text:
UPDATE (April 21, 2026):

Updating my review based on how the situation has progressed.

While the company did eventually restore water service after multiple attempts, I later discovered that the irrigation system was also damaged during the excavation and repair process.

Specifically, irrigation pipes that were previously functioning were cut, and the irrigation control wiring was also damaged. What initially appeared to be a sprinkler issue turned out to be a cut pipe causing the leak.

I provided a detailed timeline and supporting photos/videos showing that the irrigation system was working prior to the work, and that the damage occurred during the repair process.

However, the company has taken the position that irrigation work is outside the scope and is requiring additional payment to fix the damage, rather than taking responsibility for it.

I made multiple attempts to resolve this directly and reasonably, but we have not been able to reach an agreement.

Homeowners should be aware that while the main water issue may be addressed, there may be additional risks to surrounding systems during excavation, and responsibility for resulting damage may be disputed.

UPDATE (March 28, 2026):
Updating my review to 3 stars after the issue was resolved.

The general manager Richard stepped in and worked with his team to fix the problem. They corrected the incorrect connection, repaired the pipes, and restored water service to my house.

I appreciate their effort to take responsibility and resolve the issue.

However, the initial mistake caused a complete loss of water and a very stressful experience.

I will update this review based on how the situation is handled.

reviews.author: Robyn Davis
reviews.text: Proven plumbing came out to give us an estimate for a new tankless water heater. I will update my stats shortly after having the water heater a little longer but so far so good! My only small suggestion is that technicians should have some sort of handheld vacuum so that they can clean up when they are done.

reviews.author: Stanbo Miller
reviews.text:
Hooray for Zachary C! Routine maintenance turned into an urgent situation. We contacted Proven Plumbing based on the stellar Google reviews and nothing but positive recommendations from our community FB page.  40+ year old house, time for some routine bib and spigot replacements. The scheduled the consultation for the next day and by the end of the day we had received a quote.

We accepted the quote but were planning to wait until after the freeze / ice storm to schedule the service since nothing was urgent.  About 3 weeks later we received a call from our MUD that our usage was 5x the average and our meter was running constantly and we should check for leaks. Nothing in the house, I went around the perimeter and discovered an unplanned, small pond in the corner near our gas meter. I called late in the day and Proven scheduled us for the next morning. I should point out the communication is amazing via text updates and even a call when they were running 20 minutes late.

Zachary C was our plumber and he greeted us cheerily. I had spent the previous night fretting over how they would even fix this.  Zach took at look, didn't blink,  joked about not having any ducks yet, grabbed a shovel, and got to work. I'm not sure how he dug it out so fast but just like that the pipe and leak was exposed.  He also pointed out a kink in the pipe where it entered the slab, from the original installation, and took the time to chisel out some of the slab so he could round out the pipe and make the repair on the other side of the kink.

We're extremely happy with the work and the service and we have them scheduled to come out next week to do the maintenance items.

reviews.author: Angela Copley (Angelalogy)
reviews.text:
They have a great system set up for appointments and response time. Donald was polite and knowledgeable (about plumbing) and the price for the new water heater was reasonable. Per the electrician, the disconnect box was wired incorrectly, so it was not an issue with my home's wiring. I probably should take off more stars, but I am good with the plumbing part, but think that the electrical issue did not have to happen. I understand he is not an electrician, but he should be well versed in that particular task. Oh, and they left their hose behind. I may update when I get feedback from them.

They are going to reimburse me for the electrician charge. Added back a star - I am satisfied with the follow up from the company (refund has been issued, and follow up calls were received)

I will definitely be giving Nolan and the rest of the team a call whenever I'll need some unfortunate plumbing assistance in the future.

reviews.text:
Two stars because their techs were great. Desmond, Frank, Nick and Tyler were great the seven times we saw them over the past year, but after having to clear my family out of the house multiple times for AC issues. I’m done.

We purchased a $25k American Standard system plus a $6k mini split for my garage from Elite for our new construction home. After moving in January 2025, we came home to a non functioning system after a trip in May. We had an emergency call and Frank came out and fixed the system. Clogged drain line, which after 5 months of use is apparently a maintenance issue according to them and I got to pay $447 for their services. Asked about their maintenance program, no response from anyone. System goes out 3 days later. Now it’s a sensor issue, so the tech bypasses the sensor and calls it good. No charge, but also no refund for the previous service and no response on getting on a maintenance plan. Two weeks later, system goes out again it’s a breaker issue. After getting that fixed on my own the system worked fine for the last year.

September 2025, I found water in my garage and my mini split was leaking through the wall. One of the pvc elbows wasn’t glued properly on the drain line. Elite fixed it free of charge.

June 2026 my main system suffered two major failures. Leaking coil and compressor failure. Elite confirmed this, but decided, I still got to pay the $289 off hours call, while I waited around on Father’s Day for them. Because I’m now out of my 1 year labor warranty, I was offered “a deal” on the service while the parts were covered under warranty. This is the point where I just decided that I could no longer work with this company and I was really out the price of a Honda Civic, minus the reliability.

After telling them that wasn’t good enough, their service manager Tim tried to make it right, offered to replace the parts and labor for free. If this had been the first issue, I would have taken him up on it, but I’m at a point of zero confidence in this company. Maybe I had bad luck or bad installers initially, but I decided to take care of my family and have a new unit from a different company installed.

Despite what the jingle on the hold line says, which I’m very familiar with, Elite Air Conditioning and Plumbing does not care.

reviews.author: Austin Blues
reviews.text: My handy Stan's Air Conditioning dude alerted me to water around my Hot Water Heater in the attic.  OH NO!  I reached out to my contractor for a referral and he mentioned Calixto and provided me with a number.  In no time at all a few hours later, two burly dudes came to the house and up to the attic they went.  After a little while, one of the gentleman came down and diagnosed the issue for me.  I don't exactly remember the full details, but a fix was on offer, but so was the idea of full replacement.  My heater was, I believe, 7 yrs old at this point.  The cost of the repair and the cost of a new one wasn't a big stretch for me, so I opted for a new one.  It was coming to the 8-12yr window for recommended replacement anyhow.  I was told they could be back in the morning at 8am to get the job done.  the next day, the crew showed up drained and did a full replacement, got everything working fine.  They took great care to let me know that the wood subfloor was not damaged due to the leaking heater and got me up in the attic to also confirm.  Very affable, polite, intelligent plumbers.  Did not push me at all to purchase a new one, they were perfectly happy to repair the one I had.  Yay!!.... then Oh Oh.. three days later, very luke warm water and getting cooler. I called them after my morning shower, I had to head out to the office so they interreacted with my spouse.  Within a couple of hours, my spouse texted me to let know they had come by, noticed that the pilot light some was out.  They light it, let it run through the whole cycle to make sure we got hot water again and told to let them know immediately if they same issue happens again.  Happy to say, that was a month ago now and no issues whatsoever.  These guys are going to be my plumbers from now on.  Job done!

reviews.author: Shanteka Sigers
reviews.text:
Ever heard of a smoke test? It solved TWO long standing house mysteries for me. One was the fact that despite regular and rigorous extermination services, those gigantic Palmetto/Waterbugs would still appear (dead or alive) more often than they should. The second was an intermittent foul smell in my house. I said it smelled like wet cigars. Some say it was a moldy mildew-y smell. Sometimes worse when hot. Called the HVAC folks and had the vents cleaned, biopsied some padding in the return vent, bought a fan to try to dry whatever might be wet, had plumbers looking for moisture inside the walls, went searching the crawlspace under the house to search for the source. Nothing. Fine, I'll get the smoke test.

If you need a smoke test, call Clarke Kent and ask for Travis and Joshua. I had lots of questions. Will it wreck my new interior paint job? I have cats, do they need to be boarded? Will it stink? They answered them all (no, no, no). And they use a new process that is more mist than straight up smoke and they didn't have to get up on my roof to do it. They found the source -- a sewer vent pipe joint (?) inside the wall had rotted away, leaving a significant gap for bad smells and terrifying bugs. The breech was riiiight next to the HVAC and return, therefore getting blown into the house. They went in through the HVAC closet to fix it, so I don't have a big janky hole in my office wall. Plus, while Joshua was squueeeeezed behind the HVAC, he kindly pulled out old stuff I didn't know was back there and they helped me dispose of it. I mean ... y'all. Travis has so much knowledge -- when he came to estimate the job, we wanted him to come back to do it. He gave a fair, conservative estimate because it wasn't absolutely clear that this would be a problem a smoke test could fix (but still explaining that it could increase and why). That's what you want when you're troubleshooting. Travis and Joshua were great partners for me.

And a great experience isn't just how the company treats me. Joshua might be a less experienced member of the team and Travis was kind and patient and encouraged Joshua's enthusiasm. When Joshua NAILED the location of the problem, Travis let him know what a great job he did.

I waited a few weeks to write this to be sure. I have had a drastic decrease in creepy crawlies. My house now smells like Mahogany Teakwood wall plugs. So if you have a mystery smell or unwanted visitors? Call Clarke Kent and ask for Travis and Joshua.
